dict.string: Managed settings for cmux (every channel). Keys are cmux.json key paths; capitalized keys are policy keys. Forced values lock the setting; non-forced values replace its default. Exception: agents.chats.roots adds locked roots to the user list; agents.chats.enabled and agents.chats.discovery can only be forced off.
Lists finished shell commands in History. Command lines can contain secrets.
What Go Back and Go Forward walk: places in this workspace, in this window, or the focused page's own history.
Workspaces: Go Back and Go Forward move between workspaces and top pages, and return to the tab each one last had focused. Everything: they also step through tabs and panes inside a workspace.
Each machine deletes recorded commands that are older.
Each machine deletes its oldest closed tabs, screens, workspaces and windows past this many. 0 keeps them all.
Each machine deletes closed items that are older. 0 keeps them however old they are.
Minimal has no titlebar strip; the top row moves the window.
On Hover hides Back and Forward until the pointer is over the top row. The sidebar button always shows.
Show/Hide All Windows (⌃⌥⌘.) works while another app is in front.
Start Agent (⌃⌥⌘Space) works while another app is in front. Change its key in Keyboard Shortcuts.
The layout of the New Tab page. Terminal skips the page and opens a terminal. The dots at the bottom of the page also change it.
Where Cmd-T and the + button put the new tab. New Tab to the Right in a tab's menu always puts it after that tab.
On Hover shows each tab bar's + only while the pointer is over that tab bar.
Where each pane's tab bar sits. Bottom also shows the standard title bar, so the window buttons never cover a pane.
In a browser pane with the tab bar at the top: the tab bar above the address bar, or below it.
Actions shown as buttons next to the tab bar's More button. The rest are in the More menu, where Show in Tab Bar pins them back.
Shrink narrows every tab to the minimum width before the strip scrolls. Scroll keeps tabs wide and scrolls sooner.
Widest a tab gets when the strip has room.
When the strip is crowded, every tab shrinks evenly to this width, and the selected tab stays at least this wide.
Narrowest the other tabs get before the strip scrolls. Never wider than the selected tab's minimum.
Create a new workspace in the current space instead of a tab. Hold Option to reverse this for one click.
When off, Cmd-W on a pinned tab selects the next tab and keeps the pinned tab. Close a pinned tab from its menu.
When on, Cmd-T opens a workspace in the current group and Cmd-N opens a tab. When off, Cmd-T opens a tab, or a workspace when an agent chat or a pane without tabs is focused.
Warn Before Closing a Running Program
Warn Before Closing a Working Agent
Terminals run in cmux-tui and keep running after cmux quits unless you end them.
A share of the window width, for Fixed Width new columns.
A thin bar under the columns that shows and moves the visible range.
Which pane gets focus when the focused pane closes.
Hold Command or Control for 0.30 seconds to show shortcut hints.
Show Shortcuts When Holding a Modifier
Off: a found update waits, and one click downloads and installs it.
While downloads wait, a found update shows on Settings and one click downloads it.
A downloaded update installs as cmux quits. Terminals keep running.
Earlier builds kept so you can roll back. Uses almost no disk until files change.
After an update, a card at the bottom of the sidebar links to What's New until you open or dismiss it.
Short cards from the cmux team above Settings, shown when the pointer is over the sidebar.
Off: cmux never asks the network for announcements. The request carries no identifiers.
Lets agents see and use your apps through the signed cmux Computer Use helper. macOS asks for Accessibility and Screen Recording when you first allow them.
Legacy runs the current cmux Computer Use helper. Upstream runs the new helper built on the upstream Cua Driver; macOS asks for its permissions separately.
Lets agents use the free cmux AI model while you are signed out. The first time an agent uses it, cmux proves to the Cloud service that this is a real Mac. Sign in for more models and higher limits.
Stops idle sleep while an agent on this Mac is working. Your display can still turn off, and closing the lid still puts the Mac to sleep.
Keep Mac Awake While Agents Work

So your phone can find this Mac, cmux registers with its servers this Mac's name, device ID and platform, the app's bundle ID, version and build channel, the Mac's relay address and connection key, and your account and team IDs. Workspace names, folders, full paths and terminal output go only over the encrypted link to your phone. None of that, and no branch name or repo URL, is sent to cmux servers. Exception: while “Show This Mac's Workspaces on Your Phone While It's Off” is on, cmux servers store each workspace's ID, resource ID, short ID, name, name revision, group, color, icon, pinned state, unread mark, unread count and whether it is active.
Let Your Phone Use This Mac
Off, your phone can still follow, type into and answer what's already running.
Let Your Phone Start New Workspaces
A sleeping Mac can't be reached from your phone until it wakes. Closing the lid still puts the Mac to sleep.
Keep Mac Awake for Your Phone

cmux stores this Mac's workspace names, colors and unread counts so your phone can show them while the Mac is off. A workspace name can be a folder's name. No paths, tab titles or terminal output. Turning this off deletes the copy.
Show This Mac's Workspaces on Your Phone While It's Off
An agent can start other agent sessions to work on parts of a task in parallel. They show under its session in the sidebar.
The most sub-sessions one session can have open at the same time. Closing a sub-session frees its place.
How many levels of sub-sessions can start under a session. 1 lets a session start sub-sessions that cannot start their own.
Even gives every pane in the column the same size after a split.
Off hides New Row and fits a column's existing rows into it without scrolling.
Open a Tab adds a tab to the focused pane. Split Automatically splits the largest pane, like New Pane (Auto Layout).
With Split Automatically, new browsers also get their own pane instead of a tab.
Where Cmd-N, the + button and the CLI put a new workspace in the sidebar. Pinned workspaces stay above it.
Off: one list of workspaces, and a workspace on another computer names it under its title. On: a section per computer.
A workspace you have not named shows its front tab's name: a page's title, an agent chat's title, or a terminal's title or folder. Your own name always wins.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
A word that names a command by its action id ("vs": "splitRight"). Typing the whole word in the command palette puts that command first.
Commands shown first when the command palette opens, in this order, by action id.
Show chats stored on this device. Nothing is uploaded.
Find harness chat folders automatically. When off, only the listed folders are used.
Add absolute paths to harness data folders. Protected folders are refused. Your organization can add locked folders.
The picker lists these folders under Locations, after Home and Downloads. Use full paths or ~/ paths.
Inbox lists what needs you first, with the task beside it. Changes apply at once.
Colors for cmux and its terminals. A space, workspace or terminal theme overrides it.
Colors for cmux's own pages. Every bundled theme works here, and each color meets WCAG AA contrast.
Your color changes to a theme, such as "Rose Pine/background": "#1f1d2e". The theme itself never changes; remove an entry to reset that color.
The color of selection, focus and the Send button. Theme Color takes the theme's own hue, such as Rose Pine's iris.
A public-domain painting behind the window material. Lower Opacity to reveal it. Attribution is linked above.
Choose a public-domain painting, your desktop wallpaper, or a macOS system wallpaper behind the window material.
Show the wallpaper grid and live appearance tuner while they are being integrated.
How much of the theme color covers the material behind the window.
Unset, the window follows Ghostty's background-opacity and background-blur.
How much of the desktop or wallpaper shows through the glass.
Shift the tint color around the hue wheel.
Increase or reduce the tint color intensity.
Text size of tabs, the sidebar and other controls. Terminal text has its own size.
Text size of tabs, the sidebar and other controls. Terminal text has its own size.
None removes every border, hairline and separator in the app.
How the focused pane stands out: its border, subtler tabs in the other panes, both or neither.
How the other panes' tabs draw subtler when Focused Pane marks tabs: Fade dims them, Tonal steps their text down, Quiet drops the selected pill.
The look of the window: whether panes sit in one rounded card, and where lines are drawn. Separation, Sidebar Background and the sidebar border still win when you set them.
Splits, closes, moves, zooms, column scrolls and screen switches slide into place. Off: they change at once.
A new tab grows into its place in the tab bar. Off shows it there at once.
A new workspace row opens in the sidebar. Off shows it there at once.
None stops tabs, rows and panes exactly at their place. Subtle lets them settle with a small bounce.
How panes are told apart. None draws no border or divider at all; dragging between panes still resizes them. Default: dividers inside the curved main pane, borders otherwise.
How sidebar rows, tabs and panes show work in progress.
Static draws a still, distinct shape for each state. Reduce Motion always uses Static.
Three dots take the tab's icon place while an agent works.
A spinner takes a browser tab's icon place while its page loads.
A status that asks for a style (cmux status set --style) uses it.
A shell command that runs a while shows as busy.
The widest a line of text gets, in characters (30 to 1000). On a wider window the text stays centered with margins. Wide tables and code scroll sideways in their own box.
Text fills the whole pane instead of the text width.
The text size every markdown viewer opens at. Cmd-= and Cmd-- change it in one viewer; Cmd-0 goes back to this size.
The gap after each paragraph, as a share of the text size.
Code as a share of the text size. A monospaced font looks bigger than the text font at the same size, so code is a little smaller by default.
A monospaced font installed on this Mac.
Empty uses the terminal font size. Cmd-= and Cmd-- change it in one editor.
0 computes it from the font size. A value under 8 multiplies the font size.
Tab inserts spaces. Off inserts a tab character.
Tab size and spaces follow the file's own indentation.
Opt-Z turns it on and off.
Columns where a vertical line shows.
The lines that open the scopes around the top line stay at the top while you scroll.
Zoom with Command and the Scroll Wheel
The key you hold while you click to add a cursor.
Copy the Line When Nothing Is Selected
End Files with a Newline on Save
Runs the language's formatter when one is installed.
cmux reads that editor's settings and keybindings files and never changes them. A setting you make here wins.
Same as Main Pane gives the sidebar the main pane's background. Separate shades the sidebar darker than the main pane.
A line on the sidebar's edge. Off, the edge shows a line only while you hover or drag it.
How the sections above and below the workspace list draw.
The share of the sidebar the top sections fill before they scroll.
The share of the sidebar the bottom sections fill before they scroll.
Off: the top and bottom sections never scroll and the workspace list gets smaller.
Lists tabs beneath each workspace in the sidebar.
Shows every coding agent chat on this computer, newest first, at the bottom of the sidebar.
Workspace rows show only their icon, name and unread mark, and section titles become thin lines.

Comfortable rows keep one line on taller rows with more space around them. Expanded rows show each workspace's status or folder under its name, how long ago it changed, and its pull request and computer.
Workspace rows show a separate icon for working, waiting for input, error and done. Off, a row shows a spinner while it works and a blue dot when it is ready for you.
Hides the chosen sections until the pointer is over the sidebar.
A "Did you know" card above the account button shows one cmux feature a day that you have not used yet. Each tip shows only once.
The window edge the sidebar sits on. On the right, the window buttons sit over the tab bar.
Where the spaces dots sit in the sidebar: under the window buttons or above the Settings row.
On Hover shows the spaces only while the pointer is over the sidebar, like its other buttons.
Every item: Home is Command-1, the App Store Command-2, the first workspace Command-3. Workspaces only: the first workspace is Command-1.
Goes to the last item, as in browsers, or to the ninth.
What Command-Control-] and Command-Control-[ step through.
Past the last item, the next item is the first again.
A card with details opens when the pointer rests on a workspace or a tab.
How long the pointer rests on a workspace or a tab before its card opens. While a card shows, the next one opens at once.
A player for what is playing, at the bottom of the sidebar and on the new chat page.
Workspace, theme and color changes blend from the old colors to the new ones. Off: they change at once.
How long a color change takes. 0 changes colors at once.
How a color change moves over its duration. Spring uses Spring Response and Spring Damping; Custom uses the four Bezier values.
Seconds a spring color change takes to reach its new colors.
1 arrives smoothly with no overshoot. Above 1 is slower; below 1 arrives sooner.
A control point of the Custom (Bezier) curve, as in CSS cubic-bezier().
A control point of the Custom (Bezier) curve, as in CSS cubic-bezier().
A control point of the Custom (Bezier) curve, as in CSS cubic-bezier().
A control point of the Custom (Bezier) curve, as in CSS cubic-bezier().
OKLab blends with even lightness. sRGB mixes the red, green and blue channels.
What color changes do while Reduce Motion is on in macOS.
The icon or emoji you chose for a workspace.
The terminal's title, which the shell or program sets.
The status agents and hooks report, one line each.
Set by a hook: cmux workspace status set ports <text>.
Set by a hook: cmux workspace status set pr <text>.
A progress bar under the row and the busy mark of running work.
A mark while an agent works in the workspace.
The newest line agents and scripts log: cmux workspace log append <text>.
The text of the workspace's newest unread notification.
The order of the shown items under the workspace name.
Buttons shown next to the address bar. The rest are in the More menu, where Show in Toolbar pins them back.
New browser tabs open in this engine.
An address such as https://example.com. Empty opens a blank page.
A row of bookmarks under each browser toolbar.
When an agent drives a browser tab, show its cursor, clicks and typed keys on the page. Password fields show dots.
The full uBlock Origin blocks ads and trackers in Chromium tabs. Takes effect after cmux restarts.
Frees memory; history and position are kept. Also accepts a number from 1 to 1440 in a raw profile.
Open localhost on the Workspace's Machine
The address bar searches here and asks it for suggestions.
Used when Search Engine is Custom. Put {searchTerms} where the typed text goes.
Optional. Answers in the OpenSearch suggestions format, with {searchTerms} for the typed text.
Sends what you type to the search engine for suggestions. Never addresses, files or local hosts.
Completes a site you typed before or visit often.
Shows the answer to arithmetic you type. Return copies it.
The material of the address bar. Transparent draws no fill. Clear glass shows more of what is behind it. Off uses the flat theme color.
The color over the glass, from the terminal theme. Accent is the theme's own accent color, or gray when the theme has none.
Match Theme uses the standard bar radius. Capsule rounds the ends fully. Also accepts a number from 0 to 16 in a raw profile.
A soft shadow under the glass address bar.
How much the address bar covers a see-through window. At 0 it is as see-through as the window, but never so clear that its text stops being readable.
In Chromium tabs, Download keeps Chrome's default.
In Chromium tabs, Download keeps Chrome's default.
Chromium tabs use the Command-Click setting.
When off, links you click in terminals, agent chats, Home and cmux pages open in your default browser. Shift-Command-click opens a link in the other browser.
When off, links clicked in terminal output open in your default browser.
Open Terminal Links in cmux Browser
Only these hosts open in cmux, such as example.com or *.example.com. Empty opens every host in cmux.
Hosts to Open in Embedded Browser
Links that match open in your default browser. Text matches anywhere in the URL, * and ? are wildcards, and re: starts a regular expression.
The app Open in Text Editor uses for a path: an app name, a bundle ID or the path of an app. Empty uses the app that opens source code.
A browser tab asks to save a sign-in you submit. Tabs an agent drives never ask.
Offers a generated password when a site asks for a new one, and saves it.
Lets the Passwords page write every saved password to a plain-text CSV file, after you confirm with Touch ID or your password.
When a site emails you a code or link, its tab offers it. Only on the sender's own site, never filled without your click, and never stored.
When off, location data is removed from photos and videos before they are attached.
Keep Location in Photos and Videos
Show Channels below Home in the sidebar. You can also turn it on or off from the command palette.
A small Chief floats over every app and shows agent events above it. Drag it anywhere; click it to message the Chief or reply to a session.
Used when a source clears after a timeout.
No banners or sounds between these times.
A pane typed into this recently is marked read at once. 0 turns it off.
cmux status run notifies when the command took at least this long.
Notify Even When the Terminal Is Visible
When a notification alerts while cmux isn't the active app.
Notifications from agents and cmux notify go to your cmux account's feed and can reach your iPhone.
Copy Agent Notifications to the Feed
Notifications that programs send through the terminal can contain secrets. Off sends nothing to your cmux account.
Copy Terminal Notifications to the Feed
Each request's tool and command summary goes to your own cmux feed, so your iPhone can answer it.
Send Agent Permission Requests to the Feed
A notification moves its workspace to the top of the unpinned rows, unless you are looking at its pane.
Move the Workspace to the Top
Workspace ids whose notifications are silent. Mute a workspace from its sidebar row menu.
Unfinished surfaces, such as the agent session's coverage label and Pull requests view.
Show Home as a full page instead of a workspace with the Chief docked on the left. Takes effect after cmux restarts.
Uses your gh login to read notifications and review requests on this Mac. Sign in with gh auth login first.
Seconds between GitHub refreshes. Refresh in the Inbox runs immediately.
What a file link in a reply does when the file is outside the chat's folders. Keys and .env files never open.
A web image loads from its site, which then sees that you read the reply.
The card that lists a turn's edited files, with Undo and View changes.
The ring beside the model that fills as the chat uses its context window.
The microphone beside Send in every composer, including the New Tab page.
The display size for agent chat. Cmd-0 resets it.
What a new chat may do without asking. Picking a mode in a chat sets it too, until you change this setting again.
Team enrollment token from the cmux dashboard. Signed-in users in a verified domain of the team join it; the token alone never grants membership.
Team id (team_...) that manages this device.
Refuse sign-in to any team other than ManagedTeam on this device.
Features to turn off: their UI, actions and host operations are removed.
Oldest cmux version allowed to sign in, for example 1.2.0.
Turn off automatic updates (also honored in the legacy com.cmuxterm.app domain).
Turn off anonymous telemetry, crash reports included, whatever the user chose (also honored in the legacy com.cmuxterm.app domain).
